title: Patching up the nucleus: a novel role for PMLII in nuclear envelope stability.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Listed the whole Radboud Data Repository collection over WebDAV (no login): 3,979 files, 306 GB, made of 1,340 .tif + 807 .tiff + 1,199 .nd2 microscopy images, 352 .csv, 38 .xlsx, 10 CellProfiler .cpproj pipelines. Downloaded and opened 11 files: README.txt, ABOUT.txt, MANIFEST.txt, the per-figure readme text files for Figures 1 and 8, five CellProfiler output CSVs (AJ045_LaminHoles_FilteredLaminHole.csv 125 rows x 104 cols; AJ045_LaminHoles_Nucleus.csv 23 rows; AJ045_LaminHoles_Image.csv 30 rows; AJ011_PMLdetection_FilteredPML.csv 776 rows x 103 cols; AJ011_PMLdetection_Nucleus.csv 31 rows), and four author spreadsheets (Figure 1 cell-line quantification, Figure 8b and 8d manual hole quantification, AJ045_DataSummary.xlsx).
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: The per-condition cell counts quoted in the figure legends (hundreds of cells per condition per replicate) and the biological interpretation. I did not open any .nd2 or .tif image, and did not download the 306 GB image set; the image counts come from MANIFEST.txt, not from opening the images.

a1_downloadable.note: Fully open: WebDAV served every file I requested with HTTP 200 and no credentials, licence CC BY-NC 4.0. Verified by actually downloading 11 files.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: FAIL. The per-cell phenotype (no holes / holes / lamin scar / PML patch / patch+scar) exists only as tallies per field of view in Excel, e.g. 'AJ011 HeLa WT 001: 67, 6, 0, 0, 6, total 73 cells'. There is no row per cell with a label. Per-cell annotations exist only as ImageJ Cell Counter marker dots burnt into overlay .tif images, so the label would have to be reconstructed by image processing and matched back to segmented nuclei. Experimental condition is also not a column: it is embedded in free-text filenames like '260408_AJ045_100x_HeLaFLAGPMLII_siLB1sipanPML_Dox_001-2.tif'. Verified by opening the spreadsheets and the CSVs.

a3_inputs_present.note: Inputs are present rather than referenced: 104 CellProfiler shape and intensity measurements per detected object, and the raw four-channel images (DAPI, lamin A/C, lamin B1, PML) are in the collection. Verified in the CSVs and the manifest.

a4_units_stated.note: FAIL. All size measurements are raw pixel counts with no unit column and no micron scale in the files: a lamin hole reads AreaShape_Area = 45,011 and a nucleus 1,002,940. The pixel size would have to be pulled per acquisition from .nd2 metadata, and different figures mix SoRa super-resolution and standard confocal. Verified in the CSVs.

a5_enough_rows.note: FAIL at the unit that matters. The analysis unit for a hole/patch phenotype is the nucleus, and the CellProfiler nucleus tables hold 23 to 31 nuclei per experiment file (AJ045 = 23, AJ011 = 31). Object-level rows are larger (776 PML objects, 125 filtered holes) but those objects are the detections themselves, not independently labelled examples. Even pooling every CellProfiler nucleus table across the collection would not plausibly reach the ~400 labelled rows a classification task needs. Verified by opening the tables.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: 306 GB for the image route; roughly 60-100 MB for the CSV-only route
a6_fits_laptop.note: FAIL for the only version of the project that has enough examples. The CSV tables fit easily but fail A5; the image-based version needs the 306 GB collection, which breaks the 5 GB working-set rule and the project's no-raw-imaging size filter, and a convolutional or segmentation model would need a GPU. Verified from the content-size field (306,262,082,484 bytes) and the manifest.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: The counts I could check line up: the Figure 8d spreadsheet gives AJ045 PMLII+Dox 44 no-holes vs 63 holes, total 107, matching the paper's 'n = 107' for that condition. Verified by comparing the spreadsheet to the figure legend.

a8_label_provenance.note: FAIL for the tabular route. If you use the CellProfiler tables, the only thing resembling a label (a hole exists, its area, a PML object exists) IS the output of the authors' own CellProfiler segmentation pipeline run on the same intensity images that would be your features. You would be distilling a threshold-and-filter pipeline, and the hole size is computed directly from the mask the features come from. The independent label, human scoring, is only in the aggregate spreadsheets and marker overlays.

existing_models.name: Orientation-invariant variational autoencoder for label-free nuclear envelope nucleoporation (2025, found by search; abstract/snippet only, PMC12674106)
existing_models.score_and_split: Reported 0.870 area under the receiver operating characteristic curve and 82.9% test accuracy for predicting nuclear envelope nucleoporation from 32-dimensional shape embeddings; split details not retrieved.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Not retrieved - I read only the search snippet, not the paper.

existing_models.name: ProtGPS, a protein-sequence model predicting localisation to twelve condensate types including PML bodies (Cell Research 2025, found by search; snippet only)
existing_models.score_and_split: Reported area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.83 to 0.95 across condensate classes; split details not retrieved.

existing_models.name: AI nuclear morphometry pipeline for genome instability and prognosis (npj Precision Oncology 2024, found by search; snippet only)
existing_models.score_and_split: Deep-learning nucleus detection, segmentation and classification across cancer types; numbers not retrieved.

backbone.name: None appropriate. CellPose or StarDist would segment nuclei, and a Cell Painting style image featuriser could embed crops, but both are segmenters/featurisers rather than freeze-and-head backbones, and neither solves the missing-label problem.
backbone.hardware: A convolutional model on four-channel SoRa confocal images needs a GPU; the CSV route needs none but has too few rows.

integration.partner_dataset: None usable. The data carries no gene, protein or compound identifier in any table: the only standard identifiers anywhere are three text-mined accessions in the article (UniProt P36965, antibody HPA016707), not in the data files.
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Cannot be written - there is no identifier column in any of the 352 CSVs or 38 spreadsheets to join on, so any partner resource would have to be attached by hand at the level of 'this is HeLa', which answers nothing new.

controls.positive_control: Would exist in principle: a model must recover the paper's main effect that PMLII-expressing cells have larger lamin holes than PMLI-expressing cells. But with 23-31 nuclei per experiment the effect size cannot be estimated reliably in a held-out set.
controls.negative_control: Label shuffling is runnable on the CSV tables, but meaningless given the row count.
controls.external_validation: None. No second dataset measures 'lamin hole area in PMLII-overexpressing HeLa'; the phenotype is specific to this paper's cell lines and scoring rubric.

honest_claim_h3: At best: 'using CellProfiler shape and intensity features from 23-31 HeLa nuclei per experiment, a classifier separates PMLI- from PMLII-overexpressing cells' - which is a restatement of the paper's own figure, on too few nuclei, in one cell line, from one lab, with the label produced by the same segmentation pipeline that produced the features.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use microscope images of cell nuclei to predict whether the nucleus has gaps in its protein scaffold.
plain_idea.train_on: Four-channel fluorescence images of single HeLa nuclei (DNA stain, lamin A/C, lamin B1 and PML protein), or the 104 shape and brightness measurements CellProfiler extracted from each one. I verified 23-31 nuclei per experiment file; the total across the collection is unknown but is in the low hundreds for the measurement tables.
plain_idea.predict: Whether a nucleus contains a hole in its lamina (the protein mesh lining the nuclear envelope), and how large that hole is. The true answer comes either from a human scoring the image by eye in ImageJ, or from the authors' CellProfiler segmentation of the lamin B1 channel.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Cell biologists studying nuclear envelope damage, in ageing and in cancer, currently count these holes by hand, which is slow and subjective; an automated scorer would let them screen many more conditions. Even a failure would tell them how reproducible manual hole scoring is.

more_or_better_data.why: The measurement tables hold 23-31 nuclei per experiment, versus the thousands of nuclei used to train the published nuclear-morphology models found by search. The super-resolution SoRa channel combination is distinctive, but there is too little of it to be an advantage.

confidence_score.why: There are three biological replicates per condition, so between-replicate spread could be estimated in principle, but with tens of nuclei per replicate any per-prediction confidence would be too wide to be useful, and I did not verify whether the existing models report calibration.

models_beatable.why: The nucleoporation autoencoder is 2025 and reports 0.870 area under the receiver operating characteristic curve, which is not obviously saturated, but I could not retrieve its split, and we have no comparable labelled set to beat it on.

guaranteed_improvement.why: Fails on every condition: no existing model can be run as a baseline on this data, there is no shared evaluation split, and no accessible new data joins to it because the files carry no identifier of any kind.

ml_idea: Considered and rejected: train a per-nucleus classifier (lamin hole present / absent, and hole area) from four-channel confocal images or from the authors' 104 CellProfiler features, with experiment held out. Rejected because the per-cell label is not a column - it lives only as tallies per field of view and as ImageJ marker dots burnt into overlay images - and because the measurement tables hold tens of nuclei, not thousands.

effort.compute_note: No timing done. The 40-hour estimate is for reconstructing per-cell labels: parsing condition out of free-text filenames across six naming conventions, extracting Cell Counter marker coordinates from overlay .tif images, matching markers to segmented nuclei, and resolving pixel-to-micron scale per acquisition from .nd2 metadata. 306 GB is the collection's stated content size (306,262,082,484 bytes), not a download I performed.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Open one manual-quantification spreadsheet and ask whether there is one row per cell. There is not - there are five rows of tallies per experiment. That took five minutes and killed the project.

verdict_reason: Exemplary open data (306 GB, CC BY-NC 4.0, no login, per-figure readmes, CellProfiler pipelines included) attached to a single-lab microscopy paper that was never built as a modelling resource. Part A fails four ways. A2: the per-cell phenotype label is not a column anywhere - it exists only as counts per field of view in Excel and as ImageJ marker dots burnt into overlay images, so it would have to be reconstructed by image processing, and the experimental condition sits in free-text filenames. A5: the nucleus-level tables hold 23-31 rows per experiment, far under the ~400 needed for classification; the hundreds of cells in the figure legends are hand tallies, not rows. A4: every size is a raw pixel count with no unit column and no micron scale, mixing SoRa and confocal acquisitions. A8: if you instead take the CellProfiler hole detections as labels, the label is that pipeline's own segmentation output computed from the same images as the features, which is circular. The image-based version that would have enough examples also breaks A6 at 306 GB plus a GPU. Searching also found a 2025 label-free nuclear-envelope-nucleoporation model (0.870 area under the receiver operating characteristic curve) and ProtGPS for PML-body localisation, so the obvious tasks are not untouched either.
